macros.name: define@cmdkey
macros.doc: This has the effect of defining a key macro of the form \〈prefix〉@〈family〉@〈key〉 that, when used, first saves the user input to a macro of the form \〈mp〉〈key〉 and then executes 〈function〉. 〈mp〉 is the macro prefix.

macros.name: define@cmdkey
macros.doc: This has the effect of defining a key macro of the form \〈prefix〉@〈family〉@〈key〉 that, when used, first saves the user input to a macro of the form \〈mp〉〈key〉 and then executes 〈function〉. 〈mp〉 is the macro prefix.

macros.name: define@cmdkeys
macros.doc: This repeatedly calls (an internal of) \define@cmdkey for all keys in the list of 〈keys〉.

macros.name: define@cmdkeys

macros.name: savevalue
macros.doc: Saving a value for a particular key can be accomplished by using the \savevalue command with the key name as argument.

macros.name: usevalue
macros.doc: The syntax of a pointer is \usevalue{keyname} and can only be used inside \setkeys and friends. xkeyval will replace a pointer by the value that has been saved for the key that the pointer is pointing to.
